channel.description: Events newly added to the calendar, most recent first.

item.title: Junior Ranger Hike — Wed Aug 5, 2:00 PM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
Hike with Ranger Marissa on the Maple Run Trail to participate in Junior Ranger activities and earn a Junior Ranger patch! The hike will be about 0.5 miles long on easy terrain. This program is great for elementary-aged children and home-school groups looking to get outside. All materials will be provided. Meet at the Park Office to begin.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Raymond Fisher Pond Hike — Fri Aug 7, 9:00 AM — Gorges State Park - Grassy Ridge Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Join a Park Ranger for a morning Hike down the Raymond Fisher Pond Trail.
Please be prepared for a moderate, 60 minute hike, with proper footwear and water. We will be meeting at the Rainbow Falls Trailhead area.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Skins & Skulls — Sat Aug 8, 1:00 PM — Gorges State Park - Grassy Ridge Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Have you ever wanted to feel an otter’s fur? See a bear skull? Join a Ranger to learn about the mammals that call Gorges home! Meet at the Visitor Center Classroom.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Searching for Snakes and Salamanders — Sun Aug 9, 9:30 AM — Lake James State Park
item.description:
Come along on a hike with Ranger Nichelson as we search for snakes and salamanders in their natural habitat. Just bring some water and hiking shoes. Large groups of 15+ people and childen less than 8 years old are not encouraged.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Duke Career Corps: Community Resume Review — Mon Aug 10, 10:00 AM — None
item.description:
Duke Career Corps is a new initiative jointly created by the Career and Professional Development Center at Duke's Nicholas School of the Environment and the Duke Office of Community Affairs.
The purpose of the Career Corps is to provide community members with the opportunity to have their resume reviewed as they prepare to enter the workforce and/or advance their career. Members of the OneDuke career community will volunteer their time and expertise to be a new set of eyes on your resume
Source: Duke University

item.title: Mobile Health Assessment — Mon Aug 10, 10:00 AM — None
item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Additionally, there is a goal setting and referral session with a nurse, dietitian, or fitness specialist. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Digital Accessibility Pop-Up Labs — Tue Aug 11, 10:00 AM — Carolina Union
item.description:
The POP Lab is a drop-in workspace where UNC faculty and staff can make progress with support from digital accessibility consultants. Bring your documents, course materials, websites, reports, or questions, and work at your own pace. Come by for a few minutes or stay for the full session to ask questions, explore tools, solve problems and make meaningful progress toward expanding access.
Progress Over Perfection
Progress means recognizing common barriers in the platforms you use and taking small steps to reduce them. It’s choosing web formats over PDFs, applying table headers, checking color contrast and collaborating on accessible templates so everyone can start from a strong foundation. Digital accessibility depends on steady, intentional progress, not perfection, to expand access for all.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Bring Your Own Kayak - Paddle with a Ranger (Intermediate Level) — Wed Aug 12, 8:00 AM — Carolina Beach State Park
item.description:
Join a Ranger for an intermediate-level guided paddle (~4 mi) on the Cape Fear River and learn about the plants, animals, and ecology of the area.
Participants must bring their own kayak, life jacket, and paddle or rent a kayak and gear through Paddle NC.
Meet in the Marina, next to the Paddle NC boat rental shed.
Space is limited to 10 people with a minimum age requirement of 13 years old. Registration is required. Call 910-707-6050 or email carolina.beach@ncparks.gov to register.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: America 250 - Pottery Traditions — Wed Aug 12, 4:00 PM — Gorges State Park - Grassy Ridge Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Come learn about the history of pottery in North Carolina, and make an air-dry clay creation! Meet at the Visitor Center Classroom.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Moths: The Masters of Disguise — Thu Aug 13, 10:30 AM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
Have some fun with arts and crafts to learn how moths use camouflage for survival! We will also use a butterfly sweep net to find moths in tall vegetation. This program is great for elementary-aged children and home-school groups. All materials will be provided. Closed-toe shoes are recommended. Meet in the picnic area for this program.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: A Celebration of Ants — Thu Aug 13, 4:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
There are an estimated 20 quadrillion ants on our planet and their combined weight is greater than all mammals (including 8 billion people!) and birds combined. Learn about these imporant and fascinating insects in this virtual program especially for kids ages 5-13. Register
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Nature BINGO! — Fri Aug 14, 3:00 PM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
Hike with Ranger Marissa on the Beech Tree Trail and play a game of nature BINGO! To check off our BINGO card, we will be looking for animal tracks, bugs, salamanders, different types of trees, and many other things along the trail. Small prizes will be given out if participants get BINGO! This program is great for elementary-aged children and home-school groups. All materials will be provided. Closed-toe shoes and water are recommended for the hike. The Beech Tree Trail is a one-mile loop and is considered easy. Meet in the Summit Trail parking lot for this program.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame — Fri Aug 14, 7:30 PM — Vintage Church on Moore Square in Downtown Raleigh 118 S Person St
item.description:
The sweeping, epic musical based on Victor Hugo’s timeless tale and the beloved Disney film comes to life like never before! Featuring a soaring score by Alan Menken and Stephen Schwartz, this powerful story of love, acceptance, and courage will be performed in the hauntingly beautiful Vintage Church in Downtown Raleigh. In partnership with the North Carolina Master Chorale, Theatre Raleigh is creating the expansive choir needed for this majestic, site-specific theatrical experience—truly unforgettable from start to finish.
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: Rhythm & Reels - Emma Rae Concert — Sat Aug 15, 7:00 PM — Apex Nature Park Amphitheatre
item.description:
Join us on select Saturday evenings at the Apex Nature Park Amphitheatre for a night of music and movies under the stars. Our 2026 music lineup boasts a variety of genres from soul to honky tonk, Americana and beyond! So come groove with rising star Tre.Charles, rock out with Greensboro’s Sweet Dream, and enjoy family favorite movies under the stars at #R&RApex Bring your family and friends, pack a picnic basket, and come enjoy a memorable, magical summer evening! Concerts begin at 7:00pm, movies begin at dusk. To learn more about the event visit thehalle.org!
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: Once Upon a One More Time — Sat Aug 15, 7:30 PM — De Ann S. Jones Theatre at Theatre Raleigh Arts Center
item.description:
Powered by the chart-topping hits of the undisputed Princess of Pop, Once Upon A One More Time turns our favorite fairytales upside down with a clever twist! When a fairy godmother goes rogue and plops copies of The Feminine Mystique in the laps of classic heroines, the damsels embark on a quest to rewrite their stories and redefine “happily ever after.” Performed by Theatre Raleigh ACT Performance Company students
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: Before We Knew Better Art Exhibition — Mon Aug 17, 10:00 AM — Witherspoon Student Center
item.description:
The Before We Knew Better art exhibition brings together the work of Lamar Whidbee and Chris Facey to reflect on joy, memory and the experiences that shape us early in life. The exhibition looks to childhood as a place of imagination, play and connection. Rather than seeing nostalgia as a way to escape the present, the exhibition considers how memories of joy can remind us of what still matters. Whidbee and Facey ask what we carry with us from those early years and how those experiences continue to influence our well-being, relationships and sense of self. At a time when conversations around mental health are increasingly important, the exhibition offers space to pause, reflect and reconnect with the moments that first taught us about joy.

item.title: The Media and Democracy Project - What activists can do: Fix Media Now — Mon Aug 17, 7:00 PM — Virtual event
item.description:
Link to join: https://www.mobilize.us/join/47485922/1:bef19934178fcd2caef3b99b9fa25b3d61e7c0ad0f9da1385502e1755a2c05b8/
Join the Media and Democracy Project to better understand and respond to the factors that influence public opinion, voters and democracy. Each session we will activate on a current information-related subject to help Fix Media Now.
We develop and distribute skills to navigate the Information War on truth and democracy.
We are a non-partisan all volunteer group that engages in actions to directly improve the quality of public information such as messaging, fighting disinformation, engaging in media accountability and in growing support for local journalism.
We see journalists and the media as accountable allies essential for an informed democracy, countering dangerous disinformation and propaganda and promoting the common good.
How to prepare: Bring a friend - send them the link. Activate your social networks.
https://www.mobilize.us/mediademocracyproject/eve

item.title: Bearwallow Falls Hike — Tue Aug 18, 10:00 AM — Gorges State Park - Grassy Ridge Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Why are there so many waterfalls in the Jocassee Gorges area? How did they form? Join a Ranger for a guided hike to Upper Bearwallow Falls to learn the answer to these questions and more! Be sure to bring closed toed shoes, plenty of water, and dress for the weather.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:
Join Ranger Marissa in learning about the different salamanders that call Elk Knob home. We will be searching for salamanders under logs, leaves, and rocks! All materials will be provided. Closed-toe shoes are recommended. This program is open to all ages. Meet in the picnic area for this program.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Guest Night at the Ballroom — Tue Aug 18, 7:30 PM
item.description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group Come join Melanie Dale, the Mother of Ballroom Dance in Raleigh, for a fun evening of learning the basics of some of the ballroom dances like waltz, foxtrot, swing and hustle.
New students and first-time guests are invited to learn and practice. Please come a little early so you are not left behind and we can give you a name tag. Wear business casual and shoes that do not stick to the floor. Bring a friend. You may also BYOB (beer or wine).
You might even want to have dinner at Arepa Culture downstairs before the class. The food is organic and gluten-free ... very fresh!
A Step to Gold Community Ballroom is (Located: Oak Park Shopping Center near Casa Carbone Restaurant )
Address Office : 6021 Glenwood Avenue Raleigh, NC 27612
Source: Meetup: Raleigh & Triangle Activities

item.title: Youth Mental Health First Aid (Virtual) — Wed Aug 26, 9:00 AM — Zoom
item.description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed to teach parents, family members, caregivers, teachers, school staff, peers, neighbors, health and human services workers, and other caring citizens how to help an adolescent (age 12-18) who is experiencing a mental health or addictions challenge or is in crisis. Youth Mental Health First Aid is primarily designed for adults who regularly interact with young people. This course includes 2 hours of self-paced pre-work on your own before the online training. You will receive an email with further instructions 2 weeks before the training. Click here to register!
Source: Resilient Durham NC

item.title: An Evening with Authors Tim Tyson & Mary D. Williams – Mahalia Jackson, Moving On Up a Little Higher — Thu Aug 27, 6:00 PM — NC Department of Natural and Cultural Resources
item.description:
Thurs. August 27, 2026 | 6 pm - 7:30 pm | 109 E Jones St, Raleigh, NC 27601
EVENT OVERVIEW
Join the NC Department of Natural & Cultural Resources (DNCR) on August 27 from 6:00–7:30 p.m. for a FREE, powerful and inspiring evening celebrating the life and legacy of Mahalia Jackson, widely considered the greatest gospel singer of her time and an often-overlooked leader in the American Civil Rights Movement.
This special program features Mary D. Williams, acclaimed gospel singer and scholar, and Tim Tyson, New York Times best-selling author, co-authors of the new book Mahalia Jackson, Moving On Up a Little Higher: The Story of an American Civil Rights Pioneer.
Through presentation, discussion, and moments of live performance, Williams and Tyson will discuss their groundbreaking portrait of Jackson, revealing not only her extraordinary musical gifts but also her essential influence within the Civil Rights Movement, a legacy that still resonates powerfully today.

item.title: Junior Ranger Adventure — Sat Aug 29, 10:00 AM — Holly Discovery Trail
item.description:
Become a Junior Ranger at Lake James State Park! Join a ranger for a fun, family-friendly hike along the ¾-mile Holly Discovery Trail as we explore the forest and discover the plants, animals, and natural wonders that make Lake James special.
Along the way, participants will complete activities in the official Junior Ranger Activity Book, which will be provided at the beginning of the program. After completing the activities, each child will take the Junior Ranger pledge and be officially sworn in as a Lake James State Park Junior Ranger.
This program is designed for children and families. Wear comfortable walking shoes, bring water, and be prepared to spend the hour outdoors.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Junior Ranger Adventure — Sat Sep 12, 10:00 AM — Holly Discovery Trail
item.description:
Become a Junior Ranger at Lake James State Park! Join a ranger for a fun, family-friendly hike along the ¾-mile Holly Discovery Trail as we explore the forest and discover the plants, animals, and natural wonders that make Lake James special.
Along the way, participants will complete activities in the official Junior Ranger Activity Book, which will be provided at the beginning of the program. After completing the activities, each child will take the Junior Ranger pledge and be officially sworn in as a Lake James State Park Junior Ranger.
This program is designed for children and families. Wear comfortable walking shoes, bring water, and be prepared to spend the hour outdoors.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Digital Accessibility Pop-Up Labs — Tue Sep 15, 12:00 PM — Carolina Union
item.description:
The POP Lab is a drop-in workspace where UNC faculty and staff can make progress with support from digital accessibility consultants. Bring your documents, course materials, websites, reports, or questions, and work at your own pace. Come by for a few minutes or stay for the full session to ask questions, explore tools, solve problems and make meaningful progress toward expanding access.
Progress Over Perfection
Progress means recognizing common barriers in the platforms you use and taking small steps to reduce them. It’s choosing web formats over PDFs, applying table headers, checking color contrast and collaborating on accessible templates so everyone can start from a strong foundation. Digital accessibility depends on steady, intentional progress, not perfection, to expand access for all.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Tableau I — Wed Sep 30, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Tableau is a user-friendly software application used to create static or interactive visualizations and dashboards. Examples can be found here.
Tableau’s drag-and-drop interface provides tools to build a variety of visualizations with no coding required, and visualizations can be embedded in websites by copying and pasting embed code. Attendees will get started with Tableau in this hands on workshop by learning how to import data, create basic charts and maps, make and publish dashboards, and more!
This workshop is offered by the University Library and will be led by librarian Lorin Bruckner.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom. Register here: https://calendar.lib.unc.edu/event/17236362
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Leave No Trace Hike — Sun Oct 4, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Join us for Leave No Trace Discovery Hike, a guided walk through the scenic Holly Discovery trail of Lake James State Park. This family‑friendly program introduces visitors to the seven Leave No Trace principles through simple, hands‑on examples along the trail. As we explore, you’ll learn practical ways to minimize impact and help protect Lake James for future generations. Join the Media and Democracy Project to better understand and respond to the factors that influence public opinion, voters and democracy. Each session we will activate on a current information-related subject to help Fix Media Now.
